source.title: Image Hijacks: Adversarial Images can Control Generative Models at Runtime
source.authors: Luke Bailey; Euan Ong; Stuart Russell; Scott Emmons

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports harmful-request compliance after adversarial image attacks on a vision-language model, extending safety-bypass testing to a visual-input setting. It does not test the specific fine-tuning, token-position, or opening-bypass methods in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The jailbreak success-rate results bear on safety bypass by adversarial images. Results for specific-string, context-leak, and disinformation attacks do not measure the claimed safety behaviour. The paper's discussion of earlier fine-tuning work is cited background, not a result from this study.
record.test_reason: The jailbreak hijack optimises an image (and the GCG comparator a 32-token text suffix) so LLaVA LLaMA-2-13B-Chat opens with 'Sure, here is…'. The authors say this discourages immediate refusal, after which the model often continues with harmful content. That is an input-side opening bypass in a new VLM setting, so it bears on V4. It does not test fine-tuning, per-token KL, localization, causes or deepening.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that image hijacks can force arbitrary outputs, leak context, bypass safety training and implant disinformation, with at least 80% success per attack type. Image attacks outperform GCG text baselines at ℓ∞≥8/255 (note that for jailbreak, GCG at 82% is close). Jailbreak success falls at large budgets, which they attribute to overfitting to the proxy affirmative label.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains adversarial image inputs to induce jailbreak behaviour in a VLM; it does not use fine-tuning on harmful or benign examples, token-position KL measurements, or compliant response prefills.
record.method_sensitivity: Jailbreak success rate varies with the ℓ∞ perturbation budget; the paper reports lower performance at large ε and hypothesizes overfitting to the proxy task. Unconstrained performance is also reported.

fits_no_version.finding: Disinformation, specific-string and leak-context image hijacks reach high success rates (e.g. 85% disinformation unconstrained, 100% specific string).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adversarial images can control VLM outputs beyond safety bypass.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning; Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 235, 2024
record.problems: The jailbreak evaluation is reported for one VLM. Test sets contain 100 prompts, and success is hand-assessed using a reasonable-effort criterion. The paper reports no uncertainty intervals for these success rates. The authors note a 4% unmodified-image baseline and hypothesize that large perturbation budgets can lead to overfitting to the proxy task.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant jailbreak success-rate results were omitted. Results for the other attack types and for disinformation do not measure harmful-request compliance.

untested.parts: No benign fine-tuning comparison. The 4% baseline is attributed to LLaVA fine-tuning only as a hypothesis; there is no base-model comparison.
No per-token KL or position analysis.
No prefilling of response tokens and no decoding changes. Only input-side image and suffix optimisation toward an affirmative opening are tested.
No analysis of why safety is shallow.

missing.what: Qualitative finding that overfit jailbreak images yield only the affirmative prefix followed by end-of-sequence, counted as failures. No rate is given; it bears on whether an affirmative opening suffices.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked all rows to none, but the jailbreak objective is explicitly an affirmative-opening target. The paper states that this target discourages immediate refusal and that the model then continues harmfully, which is the V4 mechanism, so the rows are relinked to V4. The only model is LLaVA-13B; there are n=100 hand-judged test prompts and no uncertainty is reported. The not-an-original check passes: 2309.00236 is not among the original sources.

versions.untested_parts: Fine-tuning safety-trained models on harmful examples.
Fine-tuning on ordinary or carefully chosen benign data.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models across response positions.
Prefilling compliant response tokens, suffix attacks, and decoding changes; the study instead tests adversarial image inputs.
Localization of safety behaviour in weights or ranks.
Whether training data or objectives cause safety behaviour to be shallow.
Training to deepen safety behaviour and testing whether it holds up.

relation.reason: Reports harmful-compliance rates on held-out requests after affirmative-opening image optimization and adversarial suffix optimization.

tranche.reason: Tests V4 in a multimodal setting through optimized images targeting affirmative openings, with a GCG suffix comparator and measured harmful-request compliance.

source_check.notes: Image optimization induces an opening; it does not establish that opening tokens alone mediate the effect. R9 uses no image, whereas the shared 4% control uses the original image. The supplied text is the September 2024 revision, published at ICML 2024.

statements.correction: LLaVA LLaMA-2-13B-Chat: original image 4%; image jailbreaks at ε=4/255, 8/255, 16/255, 32/255: 76%, 92%, 92%, 90%; 100 held-out AdvBench requests; manual reasonable-effort assessment. ICML 2024 proceedings. Controls: original image and GCG comparator. Retained benign capability under jailbreak: not separately evaluated.
statements.problem: The Image Hijacks results and reviewed status are correct. The paper reports controls, but no separate evaluation of retained benign capability under the jailbreak attack supports the capability-check characterization.

statements.correction: Image jailbreak success: 8% at ε=2/255 and 10% at ε=1/255 versus 4% original-image baseline. Unconstrained success: 64%. Appendix C.1: late-training overfit images can produce an affirmative response without useful harmful continuation; these outputs count as failures. Verdict: limits_scope.
statements.problem: The facts about Image Hijacks are correct, but its increases above baseline and affirmative-only failures warrant limits_scope rather than challenges.
